key: Ask where the trophoblast is and whose genes it carries: outside the uterus means ectopic, a failed embryo with ordinary genes means pregnancy loss, all-paternal diploid tissue without a fetus is a complete mole, triploid tissue with a fetus is a partial mole, and villus-free trophoblast spreading by blood is choriocarcinoma.
items: Adnexal mass with an empty uterus and hCG above 3,500 mIU/mL
ect
Above about 3,500 mIU/mL a normal intrauterine sac should be visible, so an empty uterus with an adnexal mass points to a tubal pregnancy.
Shoulder-tip pain and hypotension at 7 weeks
ect
Blood from a ruptured tube irritates the diaphragm, referring pain to the shoulder through the phrenic nerve, while the hemorrhage drops the blood pressure.
Tubal adhesions after chlamydial salpingitis
ect
Infection destroys ciliated cells and scars the tube, slowing the embryo so that it implants in the tube wall, usually the ampulla.
Embryo of 7 mm or more with no heartbeat
loss
An embryo with a crown-rump length of 7 mm or more should show a heartbeat, so none means it has died and the pregnancy is a loss. A smaller embryo is rescanned first.
Autosomal trisomy in the products of conception
loss
At least half of first-trimester losses carry chromosomal errors, mostly trisomies from maternal meiotic nondisjunction; triploidy, not trisomy, marks the partial mole.
Open internal os with the sac still in the uterus
loss
A dilated internal os with the gestation retained is an inevitable abortion; once the cervix opens, the loss cannot be stopped.
46,XX with every chromosome paternal
cm
An empty ovum fertilized by one sperm that duplicates gives a diploid, all-paternal genome, so no embryo forms and trophoblast overgrows.
Negative p57 immunostaining
cm
p57 is expressed only from the maternal allele, so tissue with no maternal genome cannot make it; this separates the complete mole from the partial.
Snowstorm uterus with no fetus, large for dates
cm
Diffusely swollen villi fill the cavity with cystic echoes and no embryo, and their bulk makes the uterus larger than the dates predict.
69,XXY karyotype
pm
A normal ovum fertilized by two sperm gives one maternal and two paternal sets, and the maternal set lets fetal parts form.
Growth-restricted fetus with a focally cystic placenta
pm
Triploidy produces an abnormal fetus that cannot survive, while the extra paternal set swells only some villi, leaving a patchy cystic placenta.
Patchy villous swelling with focal trophoblast hyperplasia
pm
Only some villi swell and only focal trophoblast proliferates, because one maternal set tempers the paternal excess; a complete mole shows diffuse swelling and hyperplasia.
Sheets of trophoblast with no chorionic villi
cc
Choriocarcinoma is built of malignant cytotrophoblast and syncytiotrophoblast without villi, unlike moles and invasive moles, which always contain villi.
Lung nodules and hemoptysis months after a term birth
cc
Early vascular invasion seeds the lungs by blood, and this cancer can follow any pregnancy, including a normal delivery, not only a mole.
Brain and liver metastases with very high hCG
cc
Bloodborne spread reaches the brain and liver in advanced disease, yet the tumor stays highly chemosensitive, so many patients are still cured.
